IIII.}}}}</noinclude>{{hwe|band.|hu{{ls}}band.|title=husband.}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to her, Thou ha{{ls}}t {{ls}}aid vvel, that I haue no hu{{ls}}band. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=18}} For thou ha{{ls}}t had fiue hu{{ls}}bands: and he vvhom thou novv ha{{ls}}t, is not thy hu{{ls}}band. this thou ha{{ls}}t {{ls}}aid truely.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=19}} The vvoman {{ls}}aith to him, Lord, I perceiue that thou art a Prophet. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=20}} {{sup|‖}} Our fathers adored in this mountaine, and you {{ls}}ay, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 12, 6. P{{ls}}. 121. 13.''}}* that at Hieru{{ls}}alem is the place vvhere men mu{{ls}}t adore. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=21}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to her, VVoman beleeue me, that the houre {{ls}}hal come, vvhen you {{ls}}hal neither in this mountaine, nor in Hieru{{ls}}alem adore the Father. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=22}} {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''4. Reg. 17, 28. 36.''}}* You adore that you knovv not: vve adore that vve knovv, for {{ls}}aluation is of the Ievves. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=23}} But the houre commeth, and novv it is, vvhen the true adorers {{ls}}hal adore the Father {{sup|‖}} in {{ls}}pirit and veritie. for the Father al{{ls}}o {{ls}}eeketh {{ls}}uch, to adore him. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=24}} God is a {{ls}}pirit, and they that adore him, mu{{ls}}t adore in {{ls}}pirit and veritie. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=25}} The vvoman {{ls}}aith to him, I knovv that {{sc|Messias}} commeth, (vvhich is called {{sc|Christ}}): therfore when he commeth, he vvil {{ls}}hevv vs al things. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=26}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to her, I am he, that {{ls}}peake with thee.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=27}} And incontinent his Di{{ls}}ciples came: and they marueiled that he talked vvith a vvoman. No man for al that {{ls}}aid, VVhat {{ls}}eeke{{ls}}t thou, or vvhy talke{{ls}}t thou vvith her?

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=28}} The woman therfore left her vvater-pot: and {{ls}}he vvent into the citie, and {{ls}}aith to tho{{ls}}e men, {{verse|chapter=4|verse=29}} Come, and {{ls}}ee a man that hath told me al things vvhat{{ls}}oeuer I haue done. Is not he {{sc|Christ}}? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=30}} They vvent forth therfore out of the citie, and came to him.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=31}} In the meane time the Di{{ls}}ciples de{{ls}}ired him, {{ls}}aying, Rabbi eate. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=32}} But he {{ls}}aid to them, I haue meate to eate which you knovv not. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=33}} The Di{{ls}}ciples therfore {{ls}}aid one to an other, Hath any man brought him for to eate? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=34}} {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aith to them, My meate is to doe the vvil of him that {{ls}}ent me, to perfit his vvorke. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=35}} Doe not you {{ls}}ay that yet there are foure moneths, and harue{{ls}}t commeth? Behold I {{ls}}ay to you, lift vp your eies, and {{ls}}ee the countries, that they are vvhite already to harue{{ls}}t. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=36}} And he that reapeth, receiueth hire, and gathereth fruite vnto life euerla{{ls}}ting: that both he that {{ls}}ovveth, and he that reapeth, may reioyce together. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=37}} For in this is the {{ls}}aying true: that it is one man that {{ls}}ovveth, and it is an other that reapeth. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=38}} I haue {{ls}}ent you to reape that vvhich you laboured not: others haue laboured, and you haue entred into their labours.
